title: Custom CRM vs Off-the-Shelf CRM
verdict: Start with an off-the-shelf CRM unless your process is genuinely unusual, you need deep integration with operations, or per-user fees across many users outweigh a one-time build.
seoTitle: Custom CRM vs Off-the-Shelf CRM: How to Decide
seoDescription: When an off-the-shelf CRM is enough and when a custom CRM pays off: process fit, integrations, user count, cost over five years and ownership.
summary: Off-the-shelf CRMs such as Zoho, HubSpot and Salesforce are quick to start and suit standard sales processes. A custom CRM is built around your exact workflow and data, with no per-user fees, but needs a larger upfront investment and ongoing support. The deciding factors are process fit, integrations and user count.

dataPoints.label: Time to start
dataPoints.value: Off-the-shelf: days to weeks. Custom: typically 8–12 weeks for a focused first release

dataPoints.label: Cost shape
dataPoints.value: Off-the-shelf: per user per month. Custom: upfront build plus maintenance

dataPoints.label: Process fit
dataPoints.value: Custom fits exactly; packaged CRMs need workarounds for unusual workflows

dataPoints.label: Integrations
dataPoints.value: Custom can connect deeply to ERP, Tally and production; packaged relies on connectors

dataPoints.label: Ownership
dataPoints.value: Custom: you own code and data. Packaged: you rent access, data exportable

body:
## A simple test

| Question | If yes, lean towards |
| --- | --- |
| Does a standard lead-to-deal pipeline describe your sales? | Off-the-shelf |
| Do 50+ people need access, including dealers or field staff? | Custom |
| Must the CRM trigger production, stock or service work? | Custom |
| Do you need it working this month? | Off-the-shelf |

See the [CRM cost guide](/cost/crm-software) and [build, buy or extend](/blog/build-buy-or-extend-choosing-software-for-a-100-person-company).

Prices and features change often; check current details before deciding.

faqs.q: Can we start packaged and go custom later?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is a common path; clean data makes the move easier.

faqs.q: Is a custom CRM hard to maintain?
faqs.a: It needs a support arrangement; agree it before building.
